exact_line_replacements.before: rationale: Hiphil of קרב means to bring near/present. Here the subject shifts naturally to the priestly handling of the offering after the worshiper brings it. 'Present' distinguishes this verb from the later נגשׁ and avoids flattening the sequence.
exact_line_replacements.after: rationale: With the stored WLC pointing, this is Hiphil perfect 3ms with a 3fs object suffix. The form does not name the priest as its subject; presenting the offering to the priest favors the offerer as agent in context. The English retains the change from second to third person. An imperative interpretation requires a separately recorded pointing decision, not an unmarked stylistic correction.

exact_line_replacements.before: rationale: 'Hiphil of נגשׁ means to bring near. Rendering it distinctly from קרב preserves the verbal sequence: the priest first receives/presents it, then brings it near to the altar.'
exact_line_replacements.after: rationale: With the stored WLC pointing, this is Hiphil perfect 3ms with a 3fs object suffix. Bringing the offering near the altar is naturally understood as the receiving priest's action in the ritual sequence, but the subject is inferred rather than explicitly named in this clause. This contextual interpretation must not be projected backward onto the preceding delivery to the priest. Main-text disambiguation remains under review.
